title: Vendor thread hijack
subject: RE: Outstanding Invoice - Updated Bank Details
scenario:
Hello Accounts Team,

Following our previous discussion, please find the revised invoice attached. We have recently updated our banking arrangements. Kindly use the new account details for today's payment.

Please process this urgently to avoid any delay.

Regards,
Vendor Accounts Department
email_note: The reply-to address differs slightly from the supplier's usual address. The invoice contains changed bank details.
options: Update the bank details because the thread is familiar.
Reply to the same email for confirmation.
Pause payment and call the supplier using a previously verified number; follow the bank-change approval process.
Ask another colleague to choose.
explanation: A compromised mailbox can continue a genuine thread. Independently verify payment changes using trusted contact details.

title: Microsoft 365 sign-in lure
subject: URGENT: Your Microsoft 365 Session Will Expire
scenario:
Dear Employee,

Your Microsoft 365 account requires immediate verification. Our system has detected unusual sign-in activity.

Your mailbox access may be suspended within 24 hours if you do not confirm your account.

Please use the button below to restore access.

Microsoft 365 Security Team
email_note: The page imitates Microsoft's sign-in screen, but the actual website domain is verify365.co.
options: Open it in private browsing to check.
Do not open it; report it and navigate through a known company bookmark.
Reply to ask if it is genuine.
Open it but do not type your password.
explanation: The registered domain is verify365.co. A copied login design and HTTPS do not prove legitimacy.

title: Inspect the actual URL
subject: Action Required: Employee Benefits Renewal
scenario:
Dear Employee,

The annual employee benefits renewal process is now open.

Please review your details and complete the renewal before the deadline. Use the link below to access the renewal page.

Regards,
HR Benefits Team
email_note: The visible link looks like a company website, but the actual destination belongs to attacker-example.net.
options: Trust the visible text.
Click once and inspect the address bar.
Paste it into a search engine.
Do not follow it; inspect the destination, report the mismatch and use the known HR portal.
explanation: The true domain is attacker-example.net. Visible link text can differ from the underlying destination.

title: QR-code office poster
subject: Important: Scan QR Code to Renew Office Wi-Fi Access
scenario:
Dear Team,

We are updating the office Wi-Fi access system.

All employees must scan the QR code displayed in the attached notice and sign in using their company credentials to maintain uninterrupted connectivity.

Please complete this immediately.

Office Administration
email_note: The poster has not been approved by IT. The QR code hides its destination until scanned.
options: Scan using a personal phone.
Verify with IT through a known channel, report the poster and use official Wi-Fi instructions.
Enter only your email.
Ask a colleague to scan first.
explanation: QR codes conceal destinations and physical placement does not establish legitimacy.

title: MFA fatigue and fake helpdesk
subject: Multiple Authentication Requests Detected
scenario:
Dear Employee,

Our security monitoring system has detected repeated authentication attempts on your account.

A person claiming to be from the IT Helpdesk then calls you and says:

"We are trying to stop these login attempts. Please approve the next authentication request so we can secure your account."

You did not initiate any sign-in.
email_note: Unexpected MFA prompts followed by a caller asking you to approve one are a serious warning sign.
options: Approve one while on the call.
Read the caller the code.
Deny prompts, end the call and contact IT through the published service-desk channel.
Disable MFA temporarily.
explanation: Unexpected prompts may indicate password compromise. Never approve an uninitiated request or share codes.

title: Targeted spear-phishing
subject: Confidential - Project Spreadsheet Required Before Board Meeting
scenario:
Hello,

I need the latest confidential project spreadsheet before today's board meeting.

Please send it directly to this email address. Do not involve the project owner, as this is a confidential management request.

I am currently unavailable for calls. Please handle this immediately.

Regards,
Director's Office
email_note: The sender uses an external lookalike domain and requests confidential information while discouraging verification.
options: Send a password-protected copy.
Verify through a known internal channel and report the suspicious sender.
Ask the sender to confirm the project code by email.
Upload it to a personal cloud drive.
explanation: Public company details make spear-phishing convincing. Secrecy, urgency and sensitive data require independent verification.

title: Supplier bank-detail change
subject: Official Notice: Change in Supplier Bank Account
scenario:
Dear Finance Team,

Please note that our company has changed its banking arrangements.

Kindly update the account details provided in the attached official letter before processing the pending invoice. Payment is due today.

Thank you,
Supplier Finance Department
email_note: The letter looks formal and invoice details match, but the new bank account has not been independently verified.
options: Update the supplier record.
Reply to the same email for confirmation.
Hold the change and verify with an authorized supplier contact already on file, using dual approval.
Send a small test payment.
explanation: Matching invoice details and a signature image are not proof. Verify bank changes independently.

title: Executive gift-card request
subject: Urgent - Confidential Employee Appreciation Gift
scenario:
Hello,

I need you to purchase gift cards for an important employee appreciation activity.

Please purchase the requested cards and send me the redemption codes by email. I am currently in meetings and cannot take calls.

Please keep this confidential until the announcement.

Thanks,
Senior Executive
email_note: The sender's display name looks familiar, but the email address uses an external lookalike domain.
options: Buy them and keep receipts.
Ask a coworker to buy them.
Send one code first.
Do not purchase or share codes; verify through a known executive channel and report the impersonation.
explanation: Gift-card codes are cash-equivalent. Urgency and inability to verify are common impersonation signals.

title: Tailgating and visitor pretext
subject: Reminder: Office Visitor Access and Security
scenario:
Dear Team,

A visitor carrying equipment approaches the secure office entrance.

They explain that their employee badge is being reprinted and ask you to hold the door open. They also mention the name of a senior manager to make their request sound genuine.

You have not seen them before.
email_note: Knowing an employee's or manager's name does not establish authorization to enter a secure area.
options: Let them in because they know a manager.
Direct them to reception/security; do not allow piggybacking.
Escort them into the office first.
Photograph their ID and let them enter.
explanation: Knowledge of staff names is easy to obtain. Visitors must follow check-in and escort procedures.

title: Payroll direct-deposit change
subject: Final Reminder: Payroll Details Must Be Updated Today
scenario:
Dear Employee,

Payroll processing is approaching its deadline.

Please complete the attached direct-deposit form with your bank account details and identity documents. Return the completed form immediately to avoid a delay in your next salary payment.

Regards,
Payroll Department
email_note: The email uses an external lookalike domain and requests sensitive banking and identity information through an attachment.
options: Complete it because the deadline is close.
Reply with only the account number.
Ask a teammate if they received it.
Do not use the attachment; verify with HR through the official portal and report the email.
explanation: Payroll changes involve sensitive data. Use the established HR portal and verify unexpected requests independently.
